text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malawi Finance Minister Aleke Banda expressed satisfaction with the World Bank and IMF recommendations when they said the country's economy was on the right track. Banda said the World Bank/IMF report would inspire investor confidence and added that GDP deficit had dropped from 14.9 percent in 1994/5 to 5.5 percent in 1995/6.
- The Reserve Bank has announced a cut in its base lending rate to 35 percent from 45 percent as from Sept 9.

- Government has turned down a request by university students for $100,000 funding for inter-university games in southern Africa scheduled to take plce in Malawi because lecturers at two of the colleges are striking for a pay rise. The University of Malawi requested $100,000 but was only given $6,700.
- Malawi's presidential residence Sanjika Palace in Blantyre where President Bakili lives is suffering continual burglaries, despite heavy police security.
